examVariants.label: Written knowledge exam (Rules of the Road)

gdl.permitMinAge: 15 (must be enrolled in an approved driver education course)
gdl.fullLicenseMinAge: 18, or 17 after 12 months of intermediate licensing
gdl.nightCurfew: No driving 10 p.m.-6 a.m. Sun.-Thu. and 11 p.m.-6 a.m. Fri.-Sat. for drivers under 18 (with exceptions)
gdl.passengerLimits: First 12 months (or until age 18): no more than 1 passenger under age 20, unless the additional passengers are siblings

requiredDocuments: Proof of identity and date of birth (e.g. birth certificate or valid U.S. passport)
Proof of Social Security number (or ineligibility)
For applicants under 18: proof of school enrollment and driver education completion (or enrollment)
process.realIdNotes: REAL ID is optional in Illinois. It requires one document proving identity, one proving full SSN, two proving current residency, and proof of signature. A U.S. passport can be used for federal purposes instead.
process.permitFee: $20 instruction permit (verify current amount on the Illinois SOS fee schedule)
process.licenseFee: $5 for ages 18-20; $30 for ages 21-68; age-based fees apply thereafter
process.visionStandard: 20/40 in at least one eye, with or without corrective lenses

facts.pointSuspensionThreshold: Suspension length is based on total points from convictions in a 12-month period (e.g. roughly 15-44 points can lead to a 2-month suspension, scaling up with more points). Three moving-violation convictions within 12 months can also lead to suspension.
facts.moveOverRule: Scott's Law (Move Over Law): change lanes away from a stopped emergency or maintenance vehicle displaying flashing lights, or reduce speed and proceed with caution if changing lanes is unsafe
facts.interstateMaxSpeed: 70 mph on rural interstates (55 mph on many urban expressways, where posted)
facts.schoolZoneSpeed: 20 mph on school days when children are present, from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m.
